title: HDMI InfoFrame (AVI)
summary: HDMI InfoFrames are metadata packets sent during the vertical blanking interval. The AVI (Auxiliary Video Information) InfoFrame: type (0x82), version (0x02), length (13), checksum, and data: scan info, bar data, active format, RGB/YCbCr, colorimetry, picture aspect ratio, active aspect ratio, IT content, extended colorimetry, quantization range, non-uniform picture scaling, video code (VIC), pixel repetition. Used for color space signaling and HDR.

structure.meaning: Checksum (sum of all bytes including header = 0 mod 256).
Scan info (2 bits), bar data (2 bits), active format (1 bit), RGB/YCbCr (2 bits).
Colorimetry (2 bits), picture aspect ratio (2 bits), active aspect ratio (4 bits).
IT content (1 bit), extended colorimetry (3 bits), quantization range (2 bits), non-uniform picture scaling (2 bits).
Video code (VIC) (7 bits) + pixel repetition (4 bits, in byte 4).
Video Identification Code: identifies the resolution/timing (e.g., 16 = 1080p60, 97 = 4K60, 118 = 4K120).

notes: HDMI InfoFrames are sent in the vertical blanking interval (VBI).
AVI InfoFrame carries color space, aspect ratio, and VIC (resolution).
Audio InfoFrame (type 0x84) carries audio channel count and coding type.
HDMI 2.1 adds Dynamic HDR, VRR (Variable Refresh Rate), and ALLM (Auto Low Latency Mode).
